characteristics: Governed by space and air elements.
Associated with movement, flow, communication, and change.
Qualities are light, cold, dry, rough, mobile, and subtle.
When balanced: creative, enthusiastic, energetic, and adaptable.
When imbalanced: anxious, fearful, dry skin, constipation, and insomnia.
balancing_routines: Wake up early and maintain a consistent daily schedule to ground the mobile energy.
Massage the body with warm sesame oil (Abhyanga) before bathing to reduce dryness and coldness.
Eat warm, cooked, moist, and grounding meals (such as soups and stews) with healthy fats like ghee.
Practice alternate nostril breathing (Nadi Shodhana Pranayama) to calm the nervous system.

characteristics: Governed by fire and water elements.
Associated with transformation, digestion, metabolism, and energy production.
Qualities are hot, sharp, light, liquid, oily, and spreading.
When balanced: intelligent, focused, organized, and courageous.
When imbalanced: irritable, angry, prone to inflammation, acid reflux, and skin rashes.
balancing_routines: Incorporate cooling foods into the diet (sweet fruits, leafy greens, cucumber, coconut water).
Perform a gentle massage using cooling oils (like coconut or sunflower oil) to soothe excess heat.
Avoid intense exercise during the hottest parts of the day; prefer calming walks in nature.
Practice sheetali pranayama (cooling breath technique) to release heat and reduce anger.

characteristics: Governed by earth and water elements.
Associated with structure, stability, lubrication, and cohesion.
Qualities are heavy, cold, moist, slow, steady, soft, and static.
When balanced: calm, loving, compassionate, loyal, and physically strong.
When imbalanced: lethargic, prone to weight gain, congestion, attachment, and depression.
balancing_routines: Wake up before sunrise (by 6:00 AM) to prevent accumulation of heavy, sluggish energy.
Engage in vigorous daily exercise (like sun salutations or brisk walking) to stimulate circulation and heat.
Eat warm, light, dry, and spicy foods to balance coldness and moisture; minimize dairy and sweet foods.
Perform dry skin brushing (Garshana) to stimulate lymphatic flow and reduce congestion.

recipes.name: Nourishing Mung Dal Kitchari
ingredients: Pinch of salt and fresh cilantro
instructions: Wash and rinse the mung dal and rice thoroughly until the water runs clear.
In a medium pot, heat ghee on medium. Add cumin and mustard seeds; sauté until they pop.
Add turmeric and grated ginger, then add the mung dal and rice, stirring to coat.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 30 minutes until soft.
Serve warm, garnished with a pinch of salt and fresh cilantro.
recipes.description: A classic, easily digestible one-pot dish that cleanses the digestive tract and balances all three doshas.

recipes.name: Cooling Coconut Rice Pudding
ingredients: 2 tbsp maple syrup or raw sugar
instructions: Combine rice and water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then simmer covered on low for 15 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk, maple syrup, and cardamom powder.
Simmer uncovered on low heat for another 10 minutes, stirring occasionally until thick.
Garnish with shredded coconut and serve warm or at room temperature.
recipes.description: A sweet, heavy, and cooling pudding that pacifies Pitta heat and grounds Vata dryness, but can increase Kapha heaviness.

recipes.name: Warm Spiced Oatmeal
instructions: Bring water and oats to a gentle boil in a small pot.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the almond milk, cinnamon, and nutmeg; simmer for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat, let cool slightly, then stir in honey before serving.
recipes.description: A comforting, warm breakfast that stabilizes Vata and clears Kapha congestion. Slightly heating for Pitta.

recipes.name: Light Barley & Vegetable Soup
ingredients: 1 cup chopped mixed vegetables (carrots, celery, zucchini)
instructions: Heat olive oil or ghee in a large pot on medium heat. Sauté cumin and fennel powders for 30 seconds.
Add chopped vegetables and barley; stir to combine.
Pour in the vegetable broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40 minutes until barley is tender.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve warm.
recipes.description: A light, drying, and cooling soup that is excellent for reducing Kapha congestion and cooling Pitta heat. Too drying for Vata.

recipes.name: Calming Golden Milk
ingredients: 1 cup whole milk or oat milk
Pinch of black pepper (helps turmeric absorption)
instructions: Combine milk, turmeric, cardamom, black pepper, and ghee in a small saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat, stirring frequently for 5 minutes (do not boil).
Remove from heat, pour into a mug, stir in maple syrup, and drink warm before bed.
recipes.description: A deeply soothing, sleep-promoting drink that reduces systemic inflammation and supports joint and immune health.

recipes.name: Zesty Ginger-Lemon Tea
instructions: Bring water and sliced ginger root to a boil in a small pot.
Reduce heat and simmer gently for 10 minutes to extract the ginger flavor.
Strain into a cup, add lemon juice, and let cool slightly.
Stir in honey and enjoy warm.
recipes.description: An invigorating, warming drink that stimulates digestive fire (Agni), clears toxins (Ama), and reduces Vata/Kapha coldness.
